[ASSISTANT_SAID] Nordic countries such as Sweden, Finland, Norway, Denmark, and Iceland have a long history of empowering women and promoting gender equality.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] In Norway, women make up a significant portion of political leadership, with Erna Solberg serving as prime minister since 2013.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Finland's current president, Sanna Marin, is noted as the youngest female head of state in the world.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] In Sweden, women occupy 47% of the seats in parliament.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Denmark had a female prime minister, Helle Thorning-Schmidt, from 2011 to 2015.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Nordic countries have implemented policies such as quotas to promote gender equality in politics.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Middle Eastern countries have historically had limited women's participation in politics, with significant gender gaps in leadership roles.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] In Saudi Arabia, women gained the right to vote and run for office only in 2015.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] In Iran, women are not allowed to run for president, and women's representation in parliament is only 6.3%.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Cultural and religious barriers often limit women's political participation in the Middle East.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The Nordic countries have made significant progress in promoting gender equality, while Middle Eastern countries face challenges.
